key_insight: MHA2MLA-VLM provides a parameter-efficient way to convert standard multi-head attention KV caches into a compact Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA) form for vision-language models, enabling large reductions in cache size and inference cost while reusing pretrained weights without full retraining.
problem_solved: VLMs face rapidly growing Key-Value (KV) caches during multimodal inference, creating memory and compute bottlenecks; adapting existing models to MLA for cache compression without expensive pretraining has been largely unexplored.
method: Introduce lightweight, parameter-efficient conversion modules/adapters that map pretrained Multi-Head Attention (MHA) representations into a shared latent-key/value space (MLA) so original weights remain largely intact.
Design multimodal-aware latent banks and multi-head routing that compress redundant keys/values across visual and language streams, reducing KV cache footprint while preserving cross-modal alignment.

Recover accuracy with limited fine-tuning and/or distillation (instead of full pretraining), enabling plug-and-play adoption across different VLM backbones and supporting DeepSeek-style economical inference.
impact: Enables practical, low-cost deployment of large VLMs by cutting inference memory and latency from KV caches without expensive retraining; useful for real-time multimodal applications, edge/cloud scaling, and cost-sensitive research.
visual_elements: Before vs After bar chart: KV cache size and inference latency for standard MHA vs converted MLA
Architecture diagram: pretrained VLM block showing inserted MHA2MLA adapters and the latent key/value bank

paper_title: MHA2MLA-VLM: Enabling DeepSeek's Economical Multi-Head Latent Attention across Vision-Language Models
paper_authors: Xiaoran Fan, Zhichao Sun, Tao Ji, Lixing Shen, Tao Gui
